analysis.investment_thesis: A tiny ₹90 Cr micro-cap Shopify app developer riding the SME IPO euphoria — high ROE (24.8%) and zero debt are attractive, but ₹9 Cr revenue at 18.6x P/E with negative FCF for two straight years offers no margin of safety. This is a classic late-cycle small-cap where the price reflects hope, not proven durability.
key_strengths: Zero borrowings and strong ROCE of 34.3% — capital-efficient operator
Revenue grew 50% in FY25 (₹6→₹9 Cr) with EBITDA nearly doubling
High promoter holding (62.99%) — aligned skin in the game
key_risks: Micro-scale (₹9 Cr revenue) — one lost client could impair earnings materially
FCF negative in 2024 (-₹4 Cr) and 2025 (-₹2 Cr) despite positive OCF — capex/working capital eating returns
Platform dependency on Shopify ecosystem; zero moat vs. thousands of app developers
red_flags: IPO-era SME listing at cycle peak — equity base ballooned from ₹10→₹31 Cr in one year (fresh issue dilution)
Reserves jumped ₹3→₹21 Cr in FY25 = recent capital raise, untested deployment
Net profit flat YoY (₹3 Cr in both 2024 and 2025) despite revenue up 50% — margin story wobbling
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Second-level thinking asks: what does ₹90 Cr market cap for a ₹3 Cr PAT business really price in? At ~30x earnings, the market is extrapolating hyper-growth into perpetuity for a sub-scale Shopify shop with no proprietary IP, no switching costs, and no demonstrated pricing power. The ₹21 Cr reserve jump signals a recent SME IPO — textbook cycle-peak behavior where retail euphoria bids up tiny floats to absurd multiples. When sentiment reverses, such micro-caps lose 60-80% with no bid.

The fundamentals are not bad — zero debt, high ROCE, growing top line — but the margin of safety is absent. Downside case: revenue stalls at ₹9-10 Cr, PAT compresses to ₹2 Cr, and the stock re-rates to 10-12x ≈ ₹20-24 Cr mcap (75% drawdown). Upside case requires flawless execution to ₹30 Cr revenue in 3 years, which earns perhaps a double. Asymmetric in the wrong direction. Pass.
